crm_notes: POC focused on Dedicated capacity to replace parts of internal GPU fleet. Customer repeatedly emphasizes: "predictable p95/p99 during market open". Wants reserved GPU planning (monthly commit) plus burst capacity for peaks. Cost sensitivity moderate — willing to commit for guaranteed latency. Notes from calls are fragmentary: - "needs 99th percentile < 250ms for 2k token chat path at sustained 200 qps" - "will accept quantized model if accuracy delta < 0.5%" - internal ops: on-call rotation for inference faults. Legal wants a simple SLA table first pass. SE recommended continuous KV cache + per-route batching. Customer asked for pricing for 8-12 A100 equivalent reserved GPUs + 2 surge nodes.
poc_scope: Benchmarks to run in Dedicated POC: 1) Steady-state throughput ramp to target sustained QPS (50/100/200 qps) 2) 48h soak at 70% of target to surface memory leakage/temperature throttling 3) Spike/burst tests (2x, 5x) with autoscale and fallback routing to lower-cost variants 4) Canary latency SLA validation (p95/p99) across model sizes and sequence lengths 5) KV cache hit-rate characterization and prefix caching impact 6) Failover test across AZs and model-variant fallback verification
benchmark_results_summary: Initial small-scale load (single node) results: GPT-like base (quantized) at batch size 8: steady throughput ~480 req/min, median latency 95ms, p95 210ms, p99 320ms for 2k token prompts. Multi-node (3-node) distributed test with continuous batching shows linear throughput scaling to ~1.4k req/min; observed variance in p99 during synthetic peak spikes (p99 up to 520ms). Soak test in progress — no OOMs yet; thermal throttling observed on one GPU under sustained 95% utilization (investigating kernel selection).
reserved_gpu_plan: Helion prefers 8 reserved units (A100-equivalent) for primary capacity with option to burst +2 units for market-open spikes. Ask: contract term 12 months, quarterly review for right-sizing. Propose buffer of +20% in initial quarter. SE recommends ability to convert 2 reserved units to private tenancy for EU-resident workloads.
sla_requirements: Customer requests: - Availability SLA: 99.9% monthly for inference endpoints - Latency SLOs: p95 < 200ms, p99 < 350ms for 2k token chat at committed throughput; peak window exception window to be negotiated - Production incident response: 1h critical, 4h high - Audit logs and retention: 1 year for token-level cost traces (anonymized) - Data residency: EU region options for EU customers
cost_considerations: Helion will trade longer-term commitment for lower unit price. Procurement pushing for a break-even within 9-12 months vs internal infra. Wants clear billing for burst usage and overage caps. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations to reduce per-token unit cost via batching and quantization profiles.
technical_blockers: 1) Helion's infra team requires HSM/KMS integration details for key rotation policies. 2) Need proof of consistent p99 during synthetic market-open (5x baseline) before legal signs off. 3) EU data residency confirmation for subset of production dataflows.
